testcases.Test Description: Performs default reset value verification and masked write/read consistency checks over a defined list of GPIO control/status registers. Skips read-only/write-only registers as specified by masks/skip arrays; compares read data (with read masks) to expected defaults and to expected values computed from write/read masks and defaults.
testcases.Remarks: VRRW-type or non-R/W registers are explicitly skipped via skip arrays. Addresses with read_mask_array[i] == 0 are not read, and those with write_mask_array[i] == 0 are not written. Note in test_define.c: when reading default values, DIN may read as 1 if not forced; forcing 0 can assert bit-level select and cause mismatch.
Test Steps / Procedure: Entry: test_case()
Call chk_rst_val()
In chk_rst_val(): initialize i = 0; loop for i from 0 to (CNT-1)
Compute addr = addr_array[i]
If skip_rst_array[i] == 1: continue to next i
If read_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000: continue to next i
READ: data_rd = read_reg(addr)
COMPUTE: data = (data_rd & 0xfffffffe)
COMPARE: if data == default_value_array[i] then PASS path else increment def_fail_cnt and printf mismatch
End loop of chk_rst_val()
Call chk_rd_wr()
In chk_rd_wr(): define chk_val[6] = {0xffffffff,0xaaaaaaaa,0x55555555,0xf5f5f5f5,0xA5A5A5A5,0xffff0000}
Outer loop j from 0..5: set data_wr = chk_val[j]
Inner write loop i from 0..(CNT-1): addr = addr_array[i]
If skip_array[i] == 1: continue to next i
If write_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000: continue to next i
WRITE: write_reg(addr, (data_wr & write_mask_array[i]))
Inner read/verify loop i from 0..(CNT-1): addr = addr_array[i]
If skip_array[i] == 1: continue to next i
If write_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000: continue to next i
If read_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000: continue to next i
READ: data_rd = (read_reg(addr) & read_mask_array[i])
COMPUTE: wr_n = (write_mask_array[i] ^ 0xffffffff)
COMPUTE: exp_val = ((data_wr & read_mask_array[i] & write_mask_array[i]) | (wr_n & read_mask_array[i] & default_value_array[i]))
COMPARE: if data_rd == exp_val then PASS path else increment wr_fail_cnt and printf mismatch
End loops (i, j) of chk_rd_wr()
Back in test_case(): if (def_fail_cnt > 0 || wr_fail_cnt > 0) finish(1) else finish(0)

testcases.Test Description: Configures GPIOs 8–39 for input mode and falling-edge interrupt detection. For each pin, enables the interrupt, generates a single falling edge on that pin via an external pad control address, and waits with a timeout for the interrupt. The ISR validates per-pin DIN goes low, per-pin raw and group status behavior, clears raw and group status, clears system interrupt status, and re-arms for the next pin.
testcases.Remarks: Interrupt controller lines 87/88 are enabled conditionally based on GPIO instance macros. System register interrupt enable is programmed before stimulus. The wait loop uses a bounded timeout (5000 iterations of wait_on(10)). The test sets the pad state high prior to configuration and between events to maintain a known level. Race avoidance is handled by arming the pending flag before generating the edge.
Test Steps / Procedure: Entry: test_case()
Initialize test_err = 0
Conditionally enable GIC IRQ 87 or 88 based on instance
WRITE: LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1 to enable GPIO0 or GPIO1 interrupt output
WRITE: 0xA0243ffc = 0xFFFFFFFF to drive all pads high (known state)
For i = 0..31: compute per-pin control address; WRITE: per-pin control with input enable, negedge enable, and raw clear bits set; call wait_on(10)
Loop i = 0..31:
Compute wr_val = (1 << i)
WRITE: GPIO_GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1 = wr_val to pre-clear group raw
WRITE: GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1 = wr_val to enable only this pin
call wait_on(10)
Set int_pend = 1 to arm wait
WRITE: 0xA0243ffc = 0xFFFFFFFF; call wait_on(30); then WRITE: 0xA0243ffc = bitwise-not(wr_val) to create falling edge on pin
Define timeout = 5000; While int_pend == 1 and timeout > 0: call wait_on(10); decrement timeout
If timeout == 0: printf timeout error and increment test_err
After loop completes: finish(test_err)

testcases.Test Description: Enables rising-edge interrupts on GPIOs 8–39, sets group IO control to input mode, and enables all group interrupts. For each pin, generates a single rising edge using an external pad control address while arming a pending flag, waits with a timeout, and uses the ISR to confirm group interrupt assertion, clear per-pin raw status for all pins, verify group status clears, and clear system raw status before re-enabling for the next iteration.
testcases.Remarks: Conditional enable of IRQ 87/88 depending on instance. System register interrupt enable is written before stimulus. Timeout protection in the polling loop (2000 iterations of wait_on(10)). Pending flag is armed before generating the edge to prevent race conditions. Group interrupt enable is masked within ISR during service and restored afterward.
Test Steps / Procedure: Entry: test_case()
Conditionally enable GIC IRQ 87 or 88 based on instance
WRITE: LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1 to enable GPIO0 or GPIO1 interrupt output
For i = 0..31: WRITE to per-pin control (GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8..GPIO_GP0_GPIO_39) to enable rising-edge interrupt
call wait_on(10)
WRITE: GPIO_GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP1..4 = 0x000000FF to set GPIOs 8–39 as inputs
call wait_on(10)
WRITE: GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1 = 0xFFFFFFFF to enable group interrupts
WRITE: 0xA0243ffc = 0x00000000; call wait_on(10)
Set int_pend = 1
WRITE: 0xA0243ffc = 0xFFFFFFFF to create a rising edge
Set timeout = 2000; while (int_pend == 1 and timeout > 0): call wait_on(10); decrement timeout
If timeout == 0: print timeout error, increment test_err, break
Optionally WRITE: 0xA0243ffc = 0x00000000; call wait_on(10)
After loop: finish(test_err)
